subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public OpenClaw representation should outgoing Telegram custom emoji use across the message tool and Telegram plugin: raw `<tg-emoji>` HTML, typed `entities`/`caption_entities`, a shared Markdown/rich IR custom emoji span, or a combined model?
rationale: Current main has partial raw HTML preservation, but exposing first-class custom emoji changes shared tool and channel API shape, validation, fallback behavior, and plugin compatibility.

options.title: Typed entity-capable API
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved typed custom emoji/entity representation that forwards through message tool, send, caption, reply, edit, and streaming paths while preserving HTML fallback behavior.

options.title: HTML-only support
options.body: Declare raw `<tg-emoji>` HTML the supported path and document the limits, leaving entity round-trip and plugin slash-command use cases unresolved.

options.title: Defer to broader parse-mode work
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the related Telegram formatting/config design so custom emoji support lands only with a larger channel formatting contract.

recommendation.title: Typed entity-capable API
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved typed custom emoji/entity representation that forwards through message tool, send, caption, reply, edit, and streaming paths while preserving HTML fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior maintainer review already identified the API-shape blocker and recent merged Telegram rich-message work was reviewed through this ownership path.
